prompt.context: Your client is Royal Honey, a manufacturer of premium organic honey that purchases its raw honey from a single farm in the Midwest. Despite record-high demand for high-quality organic honey nationwide, Royal Honey has experienced a gradual decline in profitability in recent years. Its CEO has come to you to determine why the company's financial state has rapidly deteriorated over the past four years and to develop a turnaround strategy for the company. The company's overall goal is to return to FY16 profitability within two years. Royal Honey sells only one product: organic golden honey. It purchases raw honey from suppliers, manufactures organic golden honey, and sells to domestic high-end grocery stores (e.g., Whole Foods) nationwide. All major competitors have also experienced declining revenue and profitability, but not to the same extent as Royal Honey.
prompt.question: Why has Royal Honey's financial state rapidly deteriorated over the past four years, and what turnaround strategy would you recommend to return the company to FY16 profitability levels within two years?

clarifying_info.q: What is Royal Honey's selling price?
clarifying_info.a: The selling price has remained consistent at $10 per pound.

clarifying_info.q: What does cost of goods include?
clarifying_info.a: Cost of goods includes raw honey, processing, manufacturing, bottling, and labeling.

clarifying_info.q: Does Royal Honey have minimum purchase obligations with its current supplier?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, Royal Honey has a minimum purchase order of 10M pounds annually with its Midwest supplier.

exhibits.shows: A stacked bar chart showing Royal Honey's revenue and expense breakdown (Cost of Goods, Sales and Marketing, Overhead, Other) in $ millions for FY16, FY17, FY18, and FY19

exhibits.shows: A stacked bar chart showing total domestic supply of raw honey (value of production in $ millions) broken down by region (Northeast, Midwest, Southeast, Southwest, West) for FY16, FY17, FY18, and FY19

data.note: Midwest declined by approximately $120M; total domestic supply declined by approximately $200M over the four-year period

exhibits.title: Potential Raw Honey Supplier Comparison
exhibits.shows: A table listing five supplier options (Current Midwest, Mexico, Brazil, South Africa, China) with available raw honey supply (pounds), raw honey cost per pound, and other cost considerations per pound

data.note: Other cost considerations includes all additional costs beyond raw honey necessary to sell finished goods (e.g., transportation, manufacturing, SG&A, etc.).

framework: Raw Honey Procurement — single Midwest supplier exposure, supply constraints, cost trends
Honey Manufacturing/Processing (Operations) — production capacity, processing efficiency
Distribution/Sales — channel mix, volume trends, pricing
Honey Market Analysis — new entrants, demand shifts (food vs consumer goods), honeybee population decline
Revenue/Cost Analysis — price vs volume decomposition, cost category trends
Environmental/Regulatory Factors — FDA considerations, bee population policies

questions.prompt: Walk through Exhibit 1. What has happened to Royal Honey's financial performance over FY16–FY19? What are the key drivers?
questions.guidance: Revenue has declined $30M (from $210M to $180M) over four years while total expenses have remained roughly stable in dollar terms (~$180M each year), causing profit to fall $25M (from $30M to ~$5M). Since selling price has stayed at $10/lb, revenue decline implies volume decline. Expenses as a percent of revenue have increased significantly. Strong candidates note that despite nationwide demand growth, Royal Honey is losing volume — pointing to a supply constraint rather than a demand problem. The objective is to recover $25M in profit to reach $30M by FY21.

math.setup: Revenue FY16=$210M, FY19=$180M. Profit FY16=$210M-$180M=$30M. Profit FY19=$180M-$175M=$5M (approx). Decline in profit =$25M.
steps: Since price = $10/lb constant, volume FY16 = $210M / $10 = 21M lbs; volume FY19 = $180M / $10 = 18M lbs
math.answer: Revenue declined $30M; profit declined $25M; volume dropped from 21M to 18M lbs despite stable pricing

questions.prompt: Walk through Exhibit 2. What does it reveal about Royal Honey's supply situation?
questions.guidance: Total domestic honey production declined ~$200M over four years. The Midwest — where Royal Honey's sole supplier is located — was hit hardest, declining ~$120M (from ~$620M to ~$500M). If asked, the interviewer explains that bee populations have been declining nationwide, with Midwest populations particularly impacted. Strong candidates connect this to Royal Honey's single-source dependency: the supplier faces production constraints and has been raising prices annually, simultaneously squeezing margin and limiting volume. The candidate should recommend exploring international procurement sources.

math.answer: Midwest honey supply fell $120M (60% of total domestic decline), severely constraining Royal Honey's single Midwest supplier

questions.prompt: Given the supply constraints, what options should Royal Honey consider to increase profitability? (Brainstorm)
questions.guidance: See brainstorming section below. Primary focus should be expanding raw honey procurement internationally. Strong candidates also flag risks: new supply agreements, international supply chains and added costs, tariffs and trade agreements, FDA regulations.

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 3, what is the optimal raw honey procurement strategy to maximize profit, assuming 30M lbs of demand in FY21 at $10/lb selling price?
questions.guidance: Calculate profit per pound for each supplier (selling price minus raw honey cost minus other costs). Rank suppliers from most to least profitable and fill demand greedily. Without the minimum purchase order constraint, optimal is China+S.Africa first, then Mexico, then fill remaining with Brazil. With the minimum purchase order constraint (10M lbs from current supplier), the mix shifts. Strong candidates identify the minimum purchase obligation and recalculate.

math.setup: Selling price = $10/lb. Total demand = 30M lbs. Profit/lb = $10 - raw honey cost - other costs. Rank: China/S.Africa ($2/lb), Mexico ($1/lb), Brazil ($0.50/lb), Current ($0.25/lb). Current supplier minimum purchase = 10M lbs.
steps: Without minimum purchase order: allocate 5M lbs China + 5M lbs S.Africa + 10M lbs Mexico + 10M lbs Brazil = (5x$2)+(5x$2)+(10x$1)+(10x$0.50) = $10M+$10M+$10M+$5M = $35M profit

With minimum purchase order of 10M lbs from current supplier: must take 10M lbs current; remaining 20M lbs = 5M China + 5M S.Africa + 10M Mexico; profit = (5x$2)+(5x$2)+(10x$1)+(10x$0.25) = $10M+$10M+$10M+$2.5M = $32.5M profit
math.answer: Optimal without minimum constraint: $35M profit. Optimal with 10M lb minimum from current supplier: $32.5M profit. Both exceed the $30M FY16 target.

brainstorming.prompt: Given that honeybee populations in the United States have been declining, resulting in limited raw honey availability and rising prices — and that Royal Honey's Midwest supplier has declining production and has raised its price annually — what should our client consider to increase profitability?

categories.name: Expand Raw Honey Procurement Sources
ideas: Expand procurement beyond single Midwest farm to source raw honey internationally (e.g., Mexico, South America)
Vertically integrate or partner internationally with new suppliers
Establish multi-supplier contracts to reduce single-source dependency

categories.name: Product and Formula Innovation
ideas: Invest in R&D to develop an animal-free honey product (e.g., lab-grown or plant-based)
Change the formulaic mixture of Royal Honey to utilize less raw honey per unit, expanding volume
Invest in R&D to develop sustainable practices/technologies that better preserve beehive populations

categories.name: Pricing Strategy
ideas: Raise the price of honey sold at stores to offset rising input costs

categories.name: Risk and Complexity Considerations
ideas: New international supply agreements require negotiation and legal work
International supply chains add logistics and lead-time complexity
Tariffs, trade agreements, and international taxes increase landed cost
FDA regulations may apply to imported honey and food safety standards
Quality control of new international suppliers

recommendation: Recommend implementing an expanded international procurement strategy, prioritizing China and South Africa (highest margin at $2/lb), then Mexico ($1/lb), while fulfilling the minimum 10M lb obligation with the current Midwest supplier
This procurement mix yields $32.5M in net income in FY21, exceeding the $30M FY16 target by $2.5M (8.3%)
risks: Establishing new international supply chains adds operational complexity and lead time
FDA regulatory compliance for imported honey
Competitor response if they pursue similar international sourcing
Continued decline of honeybee populations could further tighten global supply
Quality control risk with new, unproven international suppliers
Foreign exchange risk and changing tariff/trade agreement landscape
next_steps: Perform due diligence on new international suppliers (China, South Africa, Mexico) — quality, reliability, compliance
Establish shipping contracts and logistics partnerships for international supply chain
Expand production capacity as needed to process 30M lbs
Negotiate and formalize new supply agreements with favorable pricing and volume commitments
Monitor FDA import requirements and ensure compliance
